final_answer:
\[
\boxed{\frac{p^6(p^2-1)(p^3-1)(p^4-1)}{16}}
\]

Let \(V=\mathbb F_p^4\), so \(R=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb F_p}(V)\). Fix once and for all a nonsquare \(\delta\in \mathbb F_p^\times\).

Every subfield \(E\subset M_4(\mathbb F_p)\) of order \(p^2\) makes \(V\) a \(2\)-dimensional vector space over \(E\cong \mathbb F_{p^2}\). Hence for \(x\in E\), the matrix trace on \(V\) is twice the field trace \(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_{p^2}/\mathbb F_p}(x)\). Since \(p\) is odd, the trace-zero elements of \(E\) form a one-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-line.

Thus each \(E\) has exactly two distinguished trace-zero generators \(X,-X\) satisfying
\[
X^2=\delta I.
\]
Conversely, any \(X\in M_4(\mathbb F_p)\) with \(X^2=\delta I\) generates a field \(\mathbb F_p[X]\cong \mathbb F_{p^2}\). For two fields \(E_i,E_j\), the required condition is exactly
\[
X_iX_j=-X_jX_i
\]
for their trace-zero generators.

So we first count ordered quadruples \((X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4)\) with
\[
X_i^2=\delta I,\qquad X_iX_j=-X_jX_i\quad(i\ne j),
\]
then divide by \(2^4\), since each field contributes the two choices \(\pm X_i\).

The number of possible \(X_1\) is the size of its conjugacy class. Its centralizer is \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_{p^2})\), so
\[
N_1=\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_{p^2})|}.
\]

Fix \(X_1\). Viewing \(V\cong \mathbb F_{p^2}^2\), matrices \(X_2\) anticommuting with \(X_1\) are semilinear maps relative to the Frobenius automorphism of \(\mathbb F_{p^2}/\mathbb F_p\). The stabilizer of a fixed admissible \(X_2\) inside \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_{p^2})\) is \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)\). Hence
\[
N_2=\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_{p^2})|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}.
\]

Now fix \(X_1,X_2\). The algebra they generate is \(M_2(\mathbb F_p)\), acting on one tensor factor of
\[
V\cong \mathbb F_p^2\otimes \mathbb F_p^2.
\]
Let \(K=X_1X_2\). Then \(K^2=-\delta^2 I\), and every matrix anticommuting with both \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) has the form
\[
K\otimes C
\]
with \(C\in M_2(\mathbb F_p)\). The condition \((K\otimes C)^2=\delta I\) becomes
\[
C^2=-\delta^{-1}I.
\]
For \(X_3=K\otimes C\) and \(X_4=K\otimes D\), the remaining anticommutation condition is
\[
CD=-DC.
\]

Thus we must count ordered pairs \((C,D)\in M_2(\mathbb F_p)^2\) such that
\[
C^2=D^2=\mu I,\qquad CD=-DC,
\]
where \(\mu=-\delta^{-1}\).

If \(\mu\) is nonsquare, then \(C\) gives a copy of \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\) on \(\mathbb F_p^2\). There are
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}{|\mathbb F_{p^2}^\times|}
=p^2-p
\]
choices for \(C\), and for each such \(C\), the anticommuting \(D\)’s are Frobenius-semilinear maps with square \(\mu I\), giving \(p+1\) choices. Hence the count is
\[
(p^2-p)(p+1)=p(p^2-1).
\]

If \(\mu\) is square, say \(\mu=s^2\), then \(C=\pm sI\) gives no admissible \(D\), while the remaining \(C\)’s are conjugate to \(\operatorname{diag}(s,-s)\). There are
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}{(p-1)^2}=p(p+1)
\]
such \(C\). For each, \(D\) must be off-diagonal:
\[
D=\begin{pmatrix}0&a\\ b&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad ab=s^2,
\]
so there are \(p-1\) choices. Again the count is
\[
p(p+1)(p-1)=p(p^2-1).
\]

Therefore the number of normalized generator quadruples is
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_{p^2})|}
\cdot
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_{p^2})|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}
\cdot
p(p^2-1)
=
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|}{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|}
p(p^2-1).
\]

Using
\[
|\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb F_p)|
=p^6(p-1)(p^2-1)(p^3-1)(p^4-1),
\]
and
\[
|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)|=p(p-1)(p^2-1),
\]
this becomes
\[
p^6(p^2-1)(p^3-1)(p^4-1).
\]

Finally divide by \(2^4\), because each field has two normalized trace-zero generators. Hence the required number of ordered quadruples of fields is

\[
\boxed{\frac{p^6(p^2-1)(p^3-1)(p^4-1)}{16}}.
\]
